memory.previous_feedback_interpretation: The feedback weakens the previous assumption of a broadly smooth solvent-strength response. Diethyl succinate was measured unexpectedly early at 20/1 and 50/1, while methylpyridine and the amino ester showed very large late V2 values, so solvent response is strongly molecule-dependent. The V2-tail hypothesis is strengthened for selected heteroaromatic and donor-containing regimes, but the succinate results show that polarity alone is not sufficient to predict late retention.
memory.previous_batch_rationale: The batch forms three condition-response panels rather than isolated high-scoring points. Six succinate measurements characterize an observed early-elution anomaly, five methylpyridine measurements resolve the buildup toward a severe heteroaromatic retention tail, and five amino-ester measurements test the onset of a donor-containing V2 failure. Lower-loading points at matched strong conditions provide limited loading contrasts. Together these labels expose nonlinear and molecule-specific condition effects across distinct functional-group regimes, which should improve V1/V2 generalization beyond the currently observed failure examples.
